The appellants are aggrieved of judgment dated 5/03/2025 passed in S.T.No.108/2017 by the Second Additional Sessions Judge, Vaidhan, District Singhrouli, (M.P.) whereby both the appellants have been convicted and sentenced as under:-

It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellants that there are 2 CRA-3101-2025 general and omnibus allegations.

The present case has been filed as a counterblast because neighbourer of the victim had lodged a report against the her husband alleging that he had violated her privacy as a result of which the husband of the victim in the present case was lodged in jail.
It is pointed out that Dr. Dikchha Pandey (PW-6) has not supported the prosecution story.
The victim is married woman and merely to take revenge, she has tried to falsely implicate the present appellants.
Shri Shrivastava,, learned Government Advocate supports the impugned judgment and opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that there appears to be good chances of success in appeal, without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of jail sentence of both the appellants and release them on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.7112 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with two sureties in the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial Court for their appearance before the trial Court on 03.12.2025 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant no.1- Vinod Shah and appellant no.2-Anil Shah shall remain suspended and they 3 CRA-3101-2025 be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that there appears to be good chances of success in appeal, without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of jail sentence of both the appellants and release them on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.7112 of 2025 is allowed.
